subject: Staged review ops handbook, manager rollout & announcement cadence
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.com, marcus.lin@redwood.com, maya.srinivasan@redwood.com, lauren.bishop@redwood.com

Subject: Draft: staged manager rollout + central forms (input requested)

Team —

I'm putting together a concise ops handbook and a staged announcement plan for the upcoming annual review cycle. Goal: reduce leakage, make manager communications repeatable, and protect timing for sensitive org changes. High-level asks:

- Can each of you review the timeline below and call out conflicts by EOD Wed (12 Aug)?
- Marcus: can you share the final manager script + review form baseline (we'll need the CA/EE fields populated)?
- Laura: I want your input on escalation routing for any contested outcomes.
- Maya + Lauren: please confirm capacity for manager training sessions (30–45 min) the week before launch.

Proposed timeline (fast path):
- Aug 10–16: internal review of forms & manager script
- Aug 17: manager training (recording + live Q&A)
- Aug 18: quiet-launch to managers covering sensitive roles only
- Aug 24: full manager rollout + 1:1 scheduling opens
- Sep 7: reviews close; calibration meeting week of Sep 14

Key artifacts I'm compiling now (Drafts attached): manager_script_v1.pdf, review_form_final.xlsx, manager_training_slides.pptx. I'm also preparing a short DocuSign acknowledgement for managers to confirm they've completed the training.

Notes on sensitivity: for any role flagged as "sensitive" (legal/compliance/privileged access), we run a quiet-launch to managers and coordinate with People Ops before broader scheduling.

If no major objections, I'll lock the timeline on Aug 12 and schedule the training slot.

Thanks —
Karthik
VP, Product Operations
Redwood Inference

Karthik / Laura / Marcus —

Thanks for the invite to review. I made a small set of redlines (attached notes) and a proposed facilitator script for the manager training. A couple of quick observations from past cycles at other scale-ups: 

- Keep manager training short and prescriptive (5–7 slides + common Qs). Provide a one-pager cheat sheet for managers to keep next to their calendar.
- For quiet-launch cohorts, prepare a small FAQ for managers that covers how to answer employees' immediate questions without committing to comp outcomes.
- Recommend a single calibration panel for all orgs, with pre-read packets that include signal about distribution (no names) so managers can align on leveling.

I've uploaded my annotated deck to your Drive folder and included a sample manager FAQ. Happy to run a 30-min facilitator rehearsal on Aug 19 if useful.

Cheers,
Emma Jacobs
Principal Consultant, PeopleAdj
